subtitle: When the River Heard the Name

panels.shot: wide, low-angle tableau by a shimmering river at dawn
panels.action: Guru Nanak stands calm on the bank of the Bein with Bhai Mardana seated nearby holding his rabab, mist over the water and fields of Punjab stretching into a pale sky.

dialogue.text: In the fertile plains of Punjab, Guru Nanak and Bhai Mardana sang of one light beyond Hindu and Muslim, and a river, a town, a people were changed.

i18n.hi: उपजाऊ पंजाब में गुरु नानक और भाई मरदाना एक ही नूर गाते, न हिंदू न मुसलमान — नदी, कस्बा, लोग सब बदल गए।

panels.shot: establishing wide of Rai Bhoi di Talvandi from a gentle height
panels.action: A busy fifteenth-century Punjabi town bustles within mud-brick walls as a young Guru Nanak, simple-clad, walks quietly along a dusty lane beside Bhai Mardana with his rabab slung at his side.

dialogue.text: In 1469, at Rai Bhoi di Talvandi, a child was born into a village of fields, mosques, shrines, and caravan dust. He would be called Nanak, son of Mehta Kalu and Mata Tripta.

i18n.hi: १४६९ में राय भोई दी तलबंडी में, खेतों, मस्जिदों, दरगाहों और काफ़िलों की धूल के बीच एक बच्चा जन्मा। मेहता कालू और माता त्रिप्ता का बेटा, जिसका नाम पड़ा नानक।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in a modest household
panels.action: Inside a simple Punjabi home, a teenage Guru Nanak sits cross-legged, eyes distant yet gentle, while an older villager gestures, trying to instruct him in accounts and trade, Bhai Mardana watching with a faint smile from a corner.

dialogue.text: Merchants and elders tried to fix his mind on ledgers and grain. But Nanak was drawn to song, to silence, to the question that burned behind all things: what is true, and who belongs?

i18n.hi: सेठ-सियाणे उसे हिसाब, अनाज और बही में बाँधना चाहते थे। पर नानक का दिल लगा गीत में, सन्नाटे में, उस सवाल में: सच क्या है, अपना कौन है?

panels.shot: wide shot of Sultanpur Lodhi’s streets and fort
panels.action: Sultanpur Lodhi’s narrow bazaar winds toward a small fort; Guru Nanak, now older, walks toward the fort gate with a bundle under his arm, while Bhai Mardana threads through the crowd with his rabab.

dialogue.text: In time, Nanak went east to Sultanpur Lodhi. Under Daulat Khan Lodi, he kept the granary accounts, earning trust in a town where Afghan officers, Hindu traders and farmers shared the same dust.

i18n.hi: समय के साथ नानक पूरब, सुल्तानपुर लोधी पहुँचे। दुलत ख़ान लोदी के तले उन्होंने अनाज के खाते रखे, उस कस्बे में जहाँ अफ़ग़ान फ़ौज, हिंदू बनिए और किसान एक ही धूल बाँटते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot at the Bein riverbank at dawn
panels.action: At dawn, Guru Nanak steps into the shallow water of the Bein in simple cloth, eyes half-closed in contemplation, while Bhai Mardana sits nearby on the bank tuning his rabab as mist curls low.

dialogue.text: Each morning, before the fort, the river. Nanak bathed in the Bein and lost himself in the Name. For him, this water was not escape, but a mirror for a mind searching for the One.

i18n.hi: हर सवेरे, क़िले से पहले, नदी। नानक बैन में नहाते और नाम में डूब जाते। उनके लिए यह पानी भागना नहीं, उस एक की तलाश में मन का आईना था।

panels.shot: tight three-quarter shot of Nanak in the water, eyes closed
panels.action: Guru Nanak stands still waist-deep in the river, eyes closed, palms loosely open to his sides as soft ripples circle him and Bhai Mardana watches intently from the bank.

dialogue.text: Later Sikh tradition would say that here the river took him, that he vanished for days and heard a call: ‘There is no Hindu, there is no Muslim.’ History cannot weigh such moments, but the teaching that follows is clear.

i18n.hi: बाद की सिख परंपरा कहती है, यहीं नदी ने उन्हें लिया, वे दिनों ओझल रहे और आवाज़ सुनी: ‘न कोई हिंदू, न कोई मुसलमान।’ इतिहास ऐसे पल न तौल सके, पर आगे की सीख साफ़ है।

panels.shot: medium shot on the bank as Nanak emerges toward Mardana
panels.action: Guru Nanak walks back up the damp bank toward Bhai Mardana, water trailing from his garments, his face serene yet resolute, as Mardana rises halfway with concern and curiosity.

dialogue.speaker: guru_nanak_and_bhai_mardana
dialogue.text: Mardana, the One is in all. Our quarrels are our own.

i18n.hi: मरदाना, एक वही है जो सब में है। झगड़े हमारे अपने हैं।

panels.shot: low, intimate shot of the two seated by the riverside
panels.action: Guru Nanak and Bhai Mardana sit facing each other on the grass by the Bein; Nanak gestures gently toward the town in the distance while Mardana cradles his rabab, listening with focused eyes.

dialogue.text: Tradition remembers Nanak returning from these silences with a new resolve. He would travel and sing of one Creator, of a Name that could not be owned by Hindu or Muslim alone.

i18n.hi: परंपरा कहती है, इन खामोशियों से लौटकर नानक बदले इरादे के साथ उठे। वे चलेंगे, गाएँगे एक कर्तार का, ऐसे नाम का जो न सिर्फ़ हिंदू का है न सिर्फ़ मुसलमान का।

panels.shot: wide shot of a village square with mixed crowd
panels.action: In a village square, Guru Nanak sits on a simple mat with Bhai Mardana beside him playing the rabab, while men and women of varied dress—peasants, a Sufi, Brahman, artisan—stand or sit around, listening with thoughtful faces.

dialogue.text: With Bhai Mardana’s strings carrying his words, Nanak’s hymns spread from village to caravan, from farmers to faqirs. He spoke of justice, of honest work, of a fearless remembrance of the One.

i18n.hi: भाई मरदाना के रबाब पर उनके शब्द उड़ते गए। नानक के कीर्तन गाँव से काफ़िले, किसान से फ़क़ीर तक फैल गए। वे न्याय, सच्ची कमाई और निरभय नाम-स्मरण की वाणी गाते।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nanak addressing a small mixed group indoors
panels.action: Inside a humble courtyard, Guru Nanak sits against a wall, gesturing softly as a Muslim weaver, a Hindu shopkeeper and a young woman listen; Bhai Mardana leans on his rabab nearby.

dialogue.speaker: guru_nanak_and_bhai_mardana
dialogue.text: Do not ask of caste and creed; ask if one lives in truth.

i18n.hi: जात न पूछो, मज़हब न ताको; देखो, कोई सच में जिए है या नहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a Punjabi landscape with smoke on the horizon
panels.action: Guru Nanak and Bhai Mardana stand on a ridge under a hazy sky, looking toward a distant town where dark smoke rises, the plains dotted with scattered groups of anxious people and abandoned carts.

dialogue.text: In the 1520s, Babur’s armies reached these plains. Nanak saw the fear, the marches of soldiers, the ruin of towns. His hymns, the Babur Vani, cry out against kings who crush the poor.

i18n.hi: १५२० के दशकों में बाबर की फ़ौजें इन मैदानों तक आ पहुँचीं। नानक ने डर देखा, लंबी फ़ौजी कतारें, उजड़े गाँव। उनकी बाबर-वाणी ज़ालिम बादशाहों पर बरसती है जो ग़रीब कुचलते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of Nanak’s contemplative face, shadows of turmoil behind
panels.action: Guru Nanak’s face fills the frame, eyes sorrowful yet steady, while behind him in soft focus refugees trudge past with bundles and a soldier leads a horse, hinting at war’s chaos.

dialogue.text: He did not turn away from history. He named oppression, mourned the violated, and yet, in the same breath, called people to remember the One and to restrain their own cruelty.

i18n.hi: वे इतिहास से मुँह न मोड़े। ज़ुल्म को नाम दिया, लुटी इज़्ज़त पर रोए, और उसी सांस में लोगों को एक को याद करने और अपनी खुद की ज़्यादती रोकने को पुकारा।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Ravi river bank near Kartarpur
panels.action: On the broad bank of a river, Guru Nanak stands surveying open land and scattered huts, while Bhai Mardana beside him points toward farmers in the distance tilling fields.

dialogue.text: Around 1521, Nanak chose the banks of the Ravi near Kartarpur to settle. Here, teaching stepped out of the road and into routine: fields, song, work, and shared bread became one path.

i18n.hi: लगभग १५२१ के आस-पास, नानक ने रावी के किनारे करतारपुर को डेरा चुना। यहाँ शिक्षा ने सफ़र से निकलकर दिनचर्या का रूप लिया — खेत, गीत, मेहनत और साझा रोटी एक ही मार्ग बने।

panels.shot: busy wide shot of Kartarpur community in daily work
panels.action: A lively Kartarpur scene shows men and women together in the fields, some sowing, some carrying water, while Guru Nanak walks among them offering a steady hand, and Bhai Mardana tunes his rabab near a simple dwelling.

dialogue.text: Kartarpur grew as a sangat, a gathering. They tilled the soil, worked with their hands, and then, at day’s end, sat together. Difference in birth meant nothing beside shared labor and remembrance.

i18n.hi: करतारपुर संगत बनकर बढ़ा। वे मिट्टी जोतते, हाथों से काम करते, और दिन ढलते एक साथ बैठते। जन्म की फ़र्क़ियत, साझा मेहनत और नाम-स्मरण के आगे मिट गई।

panels.shot: interior wide of a langar hall with people seated in rows
panels.action: Inside a long, simple hall, people of many backgrounds sit in straight rows on the floor, eating from the same simple bowls, as Guru Nanak moves among them with a calm smile, and Bhai Mardana sits near a pillar with his rabab resting.

dialogue.text: From Kartarpur’s hearths grew langar, the shared kitchen. The mighty and the humble sat on the same earth, eating the same food. Truth, Nanak taught, must taste like this—plain, equal, given.

i18n.hi: करतारपुर की आँच से लंगर उठा — साझा रसोई। बड़ा हो या छोटा, सब एक ही ज़मीन पर बैठ, एक ही भोजन खाते। नानक ने कहा, सच का स्वाद ऐसा होना चाहिए — सादा, समान, बाँटा हुआ।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nanak leading an evening kirtan
panels.action: At dusk, Guru Nanak sits at the front of a gathered circle in Kartarpur, eyes closed as he sings, while Bhai Mardana sits just to his side, deeply focused, fingers moving over the strings of his rabab.

dialogue.text: Evening in Kartarpur meant kirtan. Nanak’s hymns, later preserved in the Guru Granth Sahib, rose with Mardana’s strings. People who had worked side by side now breathed in rhythm as one body.

i18n.hi: शाम का करतारपुर मतलब कीर्तन। नानक की बाणी, जो आगे चलकर गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में संजोई गई, मरदाना की तारों के साथ उठती। जो दिन भर साथ जुतते थे, अब एक ही ताल में साँस लेते।

panels.shot: close-up of Nanak dictating or reciting while a follower writes
panels.action: Guru Nanak sits under a tree, reciting steadily with an uplifted hand, while an attentive companion just off-frame writes on a manuscript, and Bhai Mardana listens with bowed head.

dialogue.text: Nanak’s words were not left to rumor. His hymns—praising the One, condemning injustice, calling for humility—were remembered and later enshrined in the Guru Granth Sahib, anchoring devotion in testimony.

i18n.hi: नानक के शब्द अफ़वाहों पर न छोड़े गए। उनकी बाणी — एक की स्तुति, अन्याय की निंदा, विनम्रता का बुलावा — याद रखी गई और गुरु ग्रंथ साहिब में स्थापित हुई, भक्ति को गवाही से जोड़े।

panels.shot: gentle medium shot of an older Nanak with followers around
panels.action: An older Guru Nanak sits on a low platform in Kartarpur, lines of age soft on his face, surrounded by a small circle of followers; Bhai Mardana, also older, sits close, rabab across his lap.

dialogue.text: As years passed, Nanak did not claim divinity. He called himself a servant, a minstrel of the One. Yet around him a new way of living gathered—a discipline of work, remembrance, and shared responsibility.

i18n.hi: साल बीतते गए, नानक ने खुद को ईश्वर न कहा। वे खुद को बस एक सेवक, एक गवैया कहे, उस एक का। पर उनके चारों ओर जीने का नया ढंग जड़ पकड़ चुका था — मेहनत, नाम-स्मरण और साझा ज़िम्मेदारी का अनुशासन।

panels.shot: wide, elevated shot of Kartarpur with the river and horizon beyond
panels.action: From above, Kartarpur’s fields, dwellings, and langar hall hug the curve of the river, with tiny figures working and gathering, as Guru Nanak and Bhai Mardana walk side by side along the riverbank toward the horizon.

dialogue.text: From the Bein at Sultanpur to Kartarpur’s fields, Nanak and Mardana turned song into community. Their legacy endures wherever people remember one light, earn by honest work, and share bread without barrier.

i18n.hi: सुल्तानपुर की बैन से लेकर करतारपुर के खेतों तक, नानक और मरदाना ने गीत को संगत बना दिया। उनकी विरासत जहाँ भी है, लोग एक नूर को याद करते, सच से कमाते, और रोटी बेपरदा बाँटते हैं।

title_i18n.en: Guru Nanak and the River That Spoke

subtitle_i18n.en: When the River Heard the Name
